title: blooloop 50 Theme Park Influencer List 2026 judges announced
summary:
blooloop is pleased to announce the judges of the 2026 blooloop 50 Theme Park Influencer List.


The ninth iteration of the List is presented in association with our good friends at SimEx-Iwerks, an industry leader creating cinematic attractions and providing a diverse portfolio of immersive films.

Sean McAllister, senior vice president of attraction development, SimEx-Iwerks, says:

"Having spent much of my career in the theme park industry, it’s especially meaningful to support the blooloop Innovation Awards and celebrate the creativity and vision that continue to move our industry forward.

"It’s an honour to recognise those shaping the future of themed entertainment."

Ella Baskerville, managing director at blooloop, says: "The theme park industry continues to see investment and growth around the world.

"This would not be possible without the creative minds, visionary leaders, storytellers, designers and technologists who continuously seek to redefine what it means to be entertained.

"The blooloop 50 Theme Park Influencer List aims to highlight this passion. It celebrates you, your colleagues and the work you do in creating the theme parks of tomorrow."

2026 judges


This year's judges are:

  • Page Thompson, president, new ventures, Universal Destinations & Experiences
  • Sean McAllister, senior vice president of attraction development, SimEx-Iwerks
  • Ella Baskerville, managing director, blooloop
  • Sian Hooper, creative director, Merlin
  • Sander de Bruijn, manager design & experience, Efteling
  • Jeanette Chen, Vice President of Merlin Group and General Manager of LEGOLAND® Shanghai Resort

To place a nomination, please click here.

You can nominate multiple individuals, including yourself, but can only nominate each person once.

Nominations are open until 9 August.

All submissions will be judged by our panel of industry experts on merit, regardless of the nominee’s location, job title, or employer.

The panel of judges will select the list of 50 individuals and the Power 10 from the most nominated people.

Now is your opportunity to nominate your friends and colleagues who are making a difference in the industry.

title: Wiegand launches Wie-Flyer suspended powered coaster ride in Montenegro
summary:
Wiegand, a family-owned manufacturer of toboggan runs, rail-mounted toboggans and stainless steel dry slides, has partnered with Lovćen National Park in Montenegro to expand its offerings with a new Wie-Flyer, which opened to visitors on 3 July.

The attraction, named Falcon Fly, enhances the region's family-friendly appeal. It follows the park's Wiegand Alpine Coaster, which opened in 2023. This went viral due to its amazing views, prompting the inquiry for a second Wiegand attraction.

Falcon Fly offers stunning views across the Bay of Kotor in the Adriatic Sea(c) Kotor Cablecar

Perched 1,316m above sea level on top of the mountain, the new addition takes visitors on a flight through the picturesque landscape of Lovćen National Park, with views over the Bay of Kotor.

Riders are suspended in a TwinSeater gondola and use a joystick to control their own speed along the course to enjoy a harmonious yet thrilling flight sensation.

Versatile flying attraction

The phased installation of the Falcon Fly started in December 2025, with a timeline that included a winter hiatus due to weather conditions.

The completed attraction extends to approximately 600 m long, in a circular course that includes two helices. With a conveying capacity of up to 500 pph, the 10 TwinSeater gondolas are equipped with continually adjustable shoulder restraints and can accommodate riders from 105 cm tall.


Falcon Fly offers a potential top speed of 30 km/h, with gondolas that swing out laterally through tight curves, frequent changes in direction, waves, and straight sections to create a flying sensation.

The Wie-Flyer can be themed to integrate with its surroundings, with a compact design that makes diverse layouts and exciting routes possible. Additionally, it can be built above or combined with other Wigand leisure products, and is suitable for installation inside or outside.

The attraction can also be used as a people mover, with several stations possible.

Other benefits include environmentally friendly electric operation, low staffing and maintenance requirements, and year-round capability.

Earlier this year, Wiegand opened a new slide and hike trail in Ehrwald, Austria. The first three of the trail's six stainless steel slides were installed by helicopter on the slope directly below the Zugspitze.

title: Chance Rides highlights collaborative approach with operators across different sectors
summary:
Chance Rides, a leading manufacturer of amusement rides, believes that every project starts with understanding the customer's operations. Whether it is working with a zoo, amusement park, FEC, or the midway, the goal is to recommend the right product for the location.

When the Kansas City Zoo was evaluating transportation options, the Chance Rides team worked closely with the zoo to understand its operational needs and identify the best fit.

The e-TRAM provided the capacity, reliability, and guest comfort it sought, helping visitors move efficiently throughout the park.

Reflecting on the experience of working with Chance Rides, a spokesperson from Kansas City Zoo says:

"I've been working with Chance Rides for a little over 10 years. What I like most about working with Chance Rides is the really good communication among the engineering, design, and sales teams. They answer our questions and help us determine what our options are."

Building strong partnerships

Building long-term relationships is key in the attractions industry. Skinner Amusement Midway has partnered with Chance Rides for decades and continues to operate the iconic Zipper. Speaking about the product, the operator says:

"The LED lighting is just awesome. It is one of the better thrill rides midway. If you don't own one, you should!"

Chance's commitment to collaboration also extends to custom ride solutions.

When Friends of Santa Ana Zoo wanted to expand the appeal of their Century Wheel, the Chance Rides team worked closely with them to reimagine the attraction.

By adding a custom Monkey Wheel and integrating a unique thatched roof design, the ride became a one-of-a-kind experience that increased capacity and enhanced the guest experience.

Executive director Cathi Decker says:

"The unique thatched roof Century Wheel by Chance has doubled our ride revenue since its opening in May 2018, therefore bringing in even more money to help the animals! After running numbers on our tram and carousel, we came up with a successful concept called 'Synergy of 3' and added our 50 Monkey Wheel, honoring our heritage.

"We have gone from a half million ride revenue to $1 million in just one year with the new Wheel! Chance was amazing to work with through the process and helped us design the perfect wheel for our zoo!"

From destination attractions to carnivals, operators call on Chance Rides for dependable products, innovative solutions, and responsive support.

Chance Rides also recently shared how its long-term support helps clients maximise their investment and deliver memorable guest experiences over the long term.

title: SeaWorld, Busch Gardens parks add Sony Pictures IPs to Halloween events
summary:
United Parks & Resorts has announced major IP experiences for Halloween at SeaWorld and Busch Gardens parks in collaboration with Sony Pictures Entertainment.

In a bid to boost its Howl-O-Scream events, United Parks & Resorts has unveiled two horror IPs for this year's events – I Know What You Did Last Summer and Anaconda.

Based on the 1997 slasher movie licensed by Sony Pictures, 'I Know What You Did Last Summer: The Final Catch' is a new haunted house at SeaWorld Orlando, SeaWorld San Diego, and SeaWorld San Antonio.

Like the film, it tells the story of a group of friends who attempt to hide a fatal accident, with SeaWorld guests able to explore horrifying recreations of several movie scenes.

See on Instagram

"We're always looking for new ways to raise the bar on immersive entertainment, and bringing I Know What You Did Last Summer to our Howl-O-Scream events is an exciting milestone for all three SeaWorld parks," said Marc Swanson, CEO of United Parks & Resorts.

"This thrilling franchise has captivated horror fans for years with its suspense and terror. Now our guests will step into that world, facing some of the same heart-pounding moments that made the film come alive."

As for Sony Pictures' 1997 film Anaconda, this is being transformed into a new haunted house at Busch Gardens Tampa Bay and Busch Gardens Williamsburg.

The experience at Busch Gardens Tampa Bay is called 'Anaconda: Fear Has No Escape', while Busch Gardens Williamsburg will offer the 'Anaconda: Dead on Arrival' haunted house.

See on Instagram

"Our fans are always looking for new and immersive scares and bringing Anaconda to our Howl-O-Scream event elevates the experience at both Busch Gardens parks," said Swanson.

"The addition of Anaconda, combined with all-new haunts and entertainment, will solidify Howl-O-Scream's spot as one of the nation's top Halloween events."

The new I Know What You Did Last Summer and Anaconda houses will debut on 11 September at all parks.

Images courtesy of United Parks & Resorts

title: Disney selects five AI startups for 2026 Accelerator programme
summary:
The Disney Accelerator has selected five AI startups for this year's cohort, spanning robotics, generative AI, and data synthesis.

Now in its 12th year, the Disney Accelerator programme is designed to speed up the growth of companies working to create new entertainment experiences for Disney fans.

This year's class is made up of:

  • FieldAI, which builds foundation models that enable different types of robots to operate safely in dynamic environments without prior maps, GPS or pre-planned routes.
  • Physical Intelligence, which is developing general-purpose AI for the physical world, with foundation models designed to allow robots and other machines to perform a wide range of tasks.
  • Promise, an AI-native studio that develops films, series and visual effects, integrating generative AI into all stages of production.
  • OpenArt, a platform reimagining fan engagement with generative AI that allows users to conversationally create ideas, characters and stories using state-of-the-art models.
  • Simile, a pioneer in the field of AI-based simulation that enables companies to explore consumer insights before making decisions.

"Each year, this program endeavors to raise the bar of what is possible for the future of Disney experiences," said Bonnie Rosen, general manager of the Disney Accelerator.

"In a time of incredible change, we move forward together by supporting Disney’s creative innovators and these founders as they share ideas and breakthroughs for storytelling."

The Disney Accelerator has selected five AI startups for this year's cohort, spanning robotics, generative AI, and data synthesis

Over the next four months, FieldAI, Physical Intelligence, Promise, OpenArt and Simile will receive investment capital and the chance to collaborate with leaders across Disney.

The programme will finish with a demo day on the Walt Disney Studio Lot in Burbank, California in early November.

Since 2014, more than 60 global companies have come through Disney Accelerator, including Epic Games, ElevenLabs, Animaj, Kahoot!, Attentive, StatusPro, and AudioShake.
